rule.description: A function hosted by one locally defined struct (first parameter that is a pointer to a record defined in the main source file) whose body performs at least 36 member accesses spanning at least 8 distinct fields of a different locally defined struct, with the envied access count at least 12 times its own host accesses plus one. This is feature envy in C: window-lifecycle logic reached through the data owner's fields by a screen- or region-level function instead of living on the struct that owns the data.

checks.description: The screen-level focus binding dispatcher seeds focus candidates, follows focus_redirect chains, probes urgency through ICCCM hints, and computes and stamps stacking layers for the focus family by reading and writing the internals of multiple ws_win records directly.
checks.detected_relation: swm_screen-hosted dispatcher -> ws_win field cluster (main, focus_redirect, focus/focus_redirect guard inputs, quirks, hints, st->layer publication, ws linkage, mapping state, ewmh_flags)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Resolving the next focus candidate, deciding urgency and re-stacking the whole focus family is per-window lifecycle logic; performed field-by-field from the keybinding driver it couples the screen dispatcher to ten interior fields of the window record, so ws_win owns none of the behavior that operates on its own state.

matches.evidence: focus(struct swm_screen *s, ...) resolves candidates across the FOCUSCYCLE, FOCUSPREV, FOCUSNEXT, FOCUSURGENT and FOCUSFREE paths: it seeds from workspace focus state, chases w->main -> focus_redirect chains inline on several distinct window variables, checks !(head->quirks & SWM_Q_IGNOREURGENT) with xcb_icccm_wm_hints_get_urgency(&head->hints), and then decides and writes the stacking layer for redirect and every related window lw of the family before stack() refresh.

checks.description: The region-level mapping refresh walk decides per window whether it must be mapped or unmapped and then performs the window's own X map/unmap transition and WM_STATE restamp inline, together with all relatedness and frame bookkeeping.
checks.detected_relation: swm_region-hosted refresh walk -> ws_win field cluster (frame, id, debug, mapped, mapping, unmapping, state, main identity, type/quirk gating)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Visibility bookkeeping for the region is legitimately the walker's job, but the transition itself - which X windows to map, the mapping counters, the paired WM_STATE restamp - belongs to the window record; re-implementing it in the walk leaves the mapping state machine duplicated outside its owner.

matches.evidence: update_region_mapping(struct swm_region *r, ...) walks &ws->winlist twice; each pass tests (!HIDDEN(w) && (w && wf && w->main == wf->main || WINDOCK(w))) and then maps or unmaps w->frame, w->id and w->debug inline, bumps w->mapping/w->unmapping, flips w->mapped and writes w->state paired with a_state property changes as XCB_ICCCM_WM_STATE_NORMAL or ICONIC.

checks.description: The screen-level hide transition performs the window's focus drop, applies the EWMH_F_HIDDEN flag flip with its iconified-list membership change, and rebuilds the window's _NET_WM_STATE property set by reading and writing the window record inline.
checks.detected_relation: swm_screen-hosted hide driver -> ws_win field cluster (focus/focus family guard inputs, ws focus mirrors, bordered and quirks, ewmh_flags, iconify_entry membership, geometry moves, id for property publication)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Dropping focus from a window, flipping its hidden flag, adjusting its floating geometry and republishing its EWMH state are the window's own transitions; doing them from the binding driver means the EWMH state machine and the iconified-list discipline live outside the struct that owns the flags and the list entries.

matches.evidence: iconify(struct swm_screen *s, ...) takes the target from win->s->focus-relative state and clears the window's own focus mirrors (setting win->s->focus and win->ws->focus / focus_raise to NULL under validation guards), guards the border path with win_notile(win) || win->ewmh_flags & EWMH_F_UNTILED || ws_floating(win->ws) || WINDOCK(win) || win_below(win), computes pending/changed from win->ewmh_flags, inserts/removes win on iconified via iconify_entry, and rebuilds the _NET_WM_STATE atom list from win's flag word before publishing on win->id.

excluded.location: spectrwm.c:map_window / unmap_window / set_win_state / unfocus_win / ewmh_apply_flags / ewmh_update_wm_state / update_win_layer
excluded.reason: These are hosted by struct ws_win (their first parameter is the window) and are the correct owner-side homes for the transition logic; their ws_win accesses are host accesses, not envy, and the rule does not flag them.

Envies struct swm_strut for struts negotiation but stays below the count conjunct (35 accesses) and close to the host in ratio; the geometry math is screen-side work, so it is intentionally outside this rule's remit.
Envies struct text_fragment but across only 6 distinct fields and inside the bar text pipeline; below the field conjunct, and unrelated to the window lifecycle cluster this case's relation models.

excluded.location: spectrwm.c:new_region / swapwin / workspace_insert / cyclews / switchlayout / maximize_toggle
excluded.reason: Workspace and layout orchestration where window writes are incidental; each measures 12-19 accesses over 4-5 distinct fields with host ratios far below the rule's ratio conjunct, so none satisfies the relation.
